best_for: Windows users who want to see which apps are using the network and when, and who would pay a few dollars a year to block the ones that misbehave.

points.title: Free shows a day of history
points.text: The free version graphs CPU, memory, disk and network traffic, flags apps that go online for the first time, and scans your network. Bandwidth and network history stop at 24 hours, alert logs cover only today, and you get one remote connection.

points.title: The firewall is the paid part
points.text: Click-to-block, Lockdown Mode, Ask to Connect and firewall profiles are Premium only, as are new-device alerts, evil twin detection, data export and the mini viewer. Premium is listed at USD 2.99 per month per license, billed yearly, for 1 to 20 PCs. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Built on Windows Firewall
points.text: GlassWire sets rules through the Windows Firewall API rather than running its own filter, which keeps it light. An app may slip through briefly if you had already allowed it directly in Windows Firewall.

points.title: Not an antivirus
points.text: The FAQ says to run it next to your antivirus, not instead of one. It tells you what is talking to the internet; it does not scan files for malware.

points.title: History stays on the PC
points.text: The FAQ says your network history never leaves the device. If Premium lapses, every PC on that subscription drops back to the free feature set.

points.title: Windows only on desktop
points.text: There is no Mac or Linux version; the FAQ says Mac work is ongoing. An Android app exists. The Windows installer is 64-bit and installs for all users, so it needs administrator rights.

points.title: Older builds kept
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 14 versions, useful if an update changes something you rely on.
